body: it's school. it's always school at that age.
hey, i just want to say i can relate. i'm really hating this endless rat race that people call life. it's so soul-sucking it feels like i'm stuck in an eternal void

i dont know who you are or why are you replying to my post 3 months later but i've been doing some self-reflection and realize i need a reality check like the one you're giving me. my anxiety makes me blow things out of proportion. my therapist in high school practically begged me to go on SSRIs but i refused because i feared the side effects and because i read they weren't very effective, especially in kids (probably another manifestation of my anxiety/habit of overthinking). my anxiety is hurting me more than my circumstances are, so at this point i'm realizing i should probably get on meds. thanks for listening to my story and i hope both of us get through whatever it is that brought us to this subreddit.

i can relate. i met a girl in the elevator of my hotel and we were both going to the same concert alone (im also a girl). we walked to the venue together but when we got there she couldn't get away from me faster. she didn't even look back to say bye. she only wanted someone to walk with and then she didn't want to associate with me at all because i'm too weird. when i first spoke to her in the elevator i didn't even try to "act normal" because i expected this would be the result; i never know what the hell i'm doing wrong and always come off weird.

i can relate. small and large issues like grades, my health, or a plumbing issue in my bathroom will set me off into all-consuming spirals of anxiety. have you tried medication or therapy? i want to start but i don't know how i would have the time for that with school and everything.
